children: , a payments and banking solutions provider,
by an investor group led by its chairman and CEO in a transaction with an enterprise value of ~$1.6B, the company said Monday.
The investor group, led by Priority Technology Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore, agreed to pay $8.05 in cash per share, representing a 65% premium to Priority Technology's

unaffected price of $4.87 on Nov. 7, 2025, the last day before the investor group's non-binding proposal was first made. It represents a 38% premium to PRTH's closing price of $5.83 on Sept. 18, 2026.
stock jumped 34% to $7.80 in Monday premarket trading.

The transaction was unanimously recommended by a special committee of independent and disinterested directors, which conducted a review process with the assistance of its independent legal and financial advisors.

"After a comprehensive evaluation of the proposal, a rigorous valuation analysis, and extensive negotiations with Tom and his affiliates, we are delivering a transaction that provides compelling and certain value to Priority’s unaffiliated stockholders," said Michael Passilla, chair of the special committee.
Priore informed the committee that he doesn't plan to sell his stake in the company to any third party, as disclosed in the Schedule 13D filed in December 2025.
The go-private deal is being financed, in part, by equity commitments from funds advised by Searchlight Capital Partners, L.P. , and isn't subject to any financing conditions.

title: Priority Technology CEO to take company private in $1.6B deal
